title: How a voice agent gets a real-time face
subtitle: The agent's speech drives a causal video model that streams a full-body avatar frame by frame, for hours.
hook: A one-step video model that can only see the past puts a live face on any voice agent, for 8 hours straight.

nodes.label: Visitor
nodes.detail: Someone on a video call or in an exhibit, like the Teddy Roosevelt Oval Office built with Microsoft for his presidential library.
nodes.tradeoff: The aim is an avatar no one can tell from a human on a video call; the speaker says that is not solved yet.

nodes.label: Customer LLM
nodes.detail: LemonSlice is an API: customers bring their own LLM, which does the thinking, and LemonSlice adds only the visual layer.
nodes.tradeoff: Long term the speaker expects a split: an end-to-end 'EQ' model for the interaction, fed by a separate 'IQ' model for reasoning and tools.

nodes.label: Agent voice
nodes.detail: Customers usually bring their own voice too. Its audio, not the text, is what drives the face, so any voice agent can become a video agent.
nodes.tradeoff: The bet is that people understand best with a visual layer, since staying locked in on voice alone is hard.

nodes.label: Audio encoder
nodes.detail: Turns the agent's speech into embeddings that steer lips, face and emotion. Audio turned out to matter most for getting expressions right.
nodes.tradeoff: Most audio encoders are trained on monotone audiobooks, so LemonSlice spends a lot of time on its own embeddings.

nodes.label: Avatar image
nodes.detail: A single image defines the avatar: photorealistic, Pixar-style or cartoon. Clothes and scene can change within the same call.
nodes.tradeoff: Earrings and water move naturally because the video model has learned how the physical world behaves.

nodes.label: Emotion engine
nodes.detail: In development: predicts from the avatar's audio and the text it is about to say which emotion or action fits this moment.
nodes.tradeoff: The model can already emote and act, but not controllably or deterministically enough to keep pace with the conversation.

nodes.label: Causal video model
nodes.detail: A video diffusion transformer trained with an attention mask so it only sees the past, then cut from about 30 denoising steps to one.
nodes.tradeoff: Looking only backward compounds errors over time; an undisclosed fix lets avatars run 8 hours straight without a reset.

nodes.label: Model harness
nodes.detail: Separate GPU and CPU threads move live data so the video never stutters, clearing queues and buffers when the user interrupts.
nodes.tradeoff: The speaker says the harness is often overlooked, and that much of the product's value lives there.

flow.text: A visitor asks Teddy Roosevelt about his greatest achievement.
The customer's LLM writes Roosevelt's answer about the Panama Canal.
The chosen voice turns the answer into speech.
Encodes the speech into expressive embeddings for lips and face.
Generates the next frames in one denoising step, looking only backward.
GPU and CPU threads stream the frames without stutter.
Sees Roosevelt answer, from an avatar that runs 8 hours without reset.

takeaways.text: Building on a world model is harder to train, but full-body movement, physics and micro-expressions come more easily.
A model that only sees its own past output compounds errors; staying stable for 8 to 16 hours is hard.
Real-time avatar video now costs about the same as a voice model, which opens up consumer uses.
